What Practitioners Actually Said About AI Code Review

Six interviews, lightly edited. The quotes carry the argument; the prose between them is scaffolding.

On review latency

The bot reviews in ninety seconds. The human still takes two days. We did not shorten the queue; we added a step to it.

This was the most common complaint, and it was not about quality.

Every suggestion is plausible. That is exactly the problem — plausible is the hardest thing to reject.

On trust

We turned off auto-approve after the second incident. Not because the model was wrong more often than us — because when it was wrong, nobody had read the diff.

— Staff engineer, payments

The dissenting view

One team reported the opposite, and their reasoning is worth preserving:

Ours catches the boring class of defect — null handling, missing await, logging a secret. That freed the humans to argue about design. Throughput went up thirty per cent and stayed up.

if (user) { await audit.log(user.token) }  // the class it catches
